chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 69 — The Fallen Angels, the Mighty Oath, and the Son of Man
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for this unit within the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is the translation base for all twenty-nine verses: the names and teachings of the fallen angelic leaders, the cosmic oath called Biqa and Akae, and the enthronement and judgment of the Son of Man. Proper names and oath terms are transliterated from the Geʽez tradition; their meanings are not supplemented. The source's movement from corrupt instruction to the created order's obedience and final judgment is retained without expansion. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: After this judgment they will be terrified and made to tremble, because they revealed these things to those who dwell on the dry ground.
verses.study: The disclosure of forbidden knowledge is itself brought into judgment. Those who made hidden destructive practices available to humanity must answer for the earthly consequences.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:5 — human wickedness spreads across the earth
Luke 12:2–3 — hidden things are ultimately brought to light

verses.text: Look at the names of those angels. These are their names: the first is Semyaza; the second, Arstiqifa; the third, Armen; the fourth, Kokabael; the fifth, Turiel; the sixth, Rumyal; the seventh, Daniel; the eighth, Nuqael; the ninth, Baraqel; the tenth, Azazel; the eleventh, Armaros; the twelfth, Betaryal; the thirteenth, Basasael; the fourteenth, Ananel; the fifteenth, Turyal; the sixteenth, Simapesiel; the seventeenth, Yetarel; the eighteenth, Tumael; the nineteenth, Tarel; the twentieth, Rumael; and the twenty-first, Izezeel.
verses.study: Naming the leaders individualizes responsibility. The rebellion was not an abstract force but the work of accountable agents whose choices are remembered.
crossReferences: 1 Enoch 6:7–8 — leaders of the descent are named
Revelation 20:12 — judgment proceeds according to recorded deeds

verses.text: These are the chiefs of their angels, the leaders over hundreds, over fifties and over tens.
verses.study: The rebels possess an ordered hierarchy, but organization does not make their cause righteous. Authority becomes culpable when it coordinates disobedience.
crossReferences: Exodus 18:21 — leaders are appointed over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens
Ephesians 6:12 — spiritual rebellion includes ranks of power

verses.text: The name of the first is Yeqon. He is the one who led all the sons of the holy angels astray, brought them down onto the dry ground and led them astray through the daughters of humanity.
verses.study: Yeqon's guilt lies in instigating a collective departure from the holy realm. Leadership is measured not only by personal action but by where it leads others.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:1–2 — heavenly sons take daughters of humanity
James 3:1 — those who lead others face stricter judgment

verses.text: The name of the second is Asbeel. He gave evil counsel to the sons of the holy angels and led them astray, so that they defiled their bodies with the daughters of humanity.
verses.study: Corruption begins in counsel before it appears in conduct. Asbeel turns deliberation toward defilement, showing the moral weight carried by persuasive advice.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:1 — blessedness refuses the counsel of the wicked
Jude 6–7 — rebellion and sexual transgression lead to judgment

verses.text: The name of the third is Gadreel. He showed the children of humanity all the blows of death; he led Eve astray, and he showed the children of humanity the weapons of death—the shield and breastplate, the sword for battle and every weapon of death.
verses.study: Gadreel joins deception with the technology of violence. Knowledge detached from obedience becomes a means by which death is multiplied.
crossReferences: Genesis 3:1–6 — Eve is deceived into disobedience
Genesis 4:22–23 — metalworking and boastful violence appear together

verses.text: From his hand they have gone out against those who dwell on the dry ground from that day and forever.
verses.study: The enduring circulation of weapons reveals how a single corrupt disclosure can outlive its teacher. Destructive systems continue to wound later generations.
crossReferences: Isaiah 2:4 — God's peace reverses the manufacture of weapons
Matthew 26:52 — those who take the sword perish by it

verses.text: The name of the fourth is Penemue. He showed the children of humanity the bitter and the sweet, and he showed them all the secrets of their wisdom.
verses.study: Penemue's teaching promises mastery of life's contrasts and hidden wisdom. The chapter condemns knowledge that crosses divinely set boundaries, not faithful discernment received in reverence.
crossReferences: Genesis 3:5–6 — forbidden knowledge is desired as wisdom
James 3:15–17 — earthly wisdom is contrasted with wisdom from above

verses.text: He taught humanity writing with ink and paper, and through it many went astray from age to age and until this day.
verses.study: Writing can preserve truth, as Enoch's own book demonstrates, yet it can also preserve and spread error. A medium's moral effect depends on the truthfulness of what it carries.
crossReferences: Jeremiah 8:8 — the lying pen can distort instruction
John 20:31 — writing can also serve life-giving faith

verses.text: For humanity was not created for this, that they should confirm their faithfulness with ink and paper.
verses.study: Faithfulness cannot be reduced to written claims. The verse calls for a lived integrity that writing may witness but cannot manufacture.
crossReferences: Jeremiah 31:33 — God's instruction is written on the heart
2 Corinthians 3:3 — living people are letters written by God's Spirit

verses.text: For human beings were not created differently from the angels, so that they might remain righteous and pure; and death, which destroys everything, would not have touched them. But through this knowledge they perish, and through its power death consumes them.
verses.study: The verse contrasts humanity's calling to purity with knowledge that empowers death. Intellectual attainment cannot replace obedience or rescue its bearer from corruption.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:17 — disobedient grasping brings death
Romans 5:12 — death enters the human world through sin

verses.text: The name of the fifth is Kasdeya. He showed the children of humanity every wicked blow of spirits and demons: the blow against the embryo in the womb so that it might be lost, the bite of the serpent, and the blow that comes at midday through the serpent named Tabaet.
verses.study: Kasdeya's teaching targets life at its most vulnerable and turns unseen powers toward harm. The catalogue presents such practices as wicked disclosures, never as legitimate wisdom.
crossReferences: Psalm 91:5–6 — God guards against terror and destruction at midday
Revelation 12:9 — the ancient serpent is associated with deception and harm

verses.text: This is the number of Kasbeel, the chief of the oath that he showed to the holy ones when he dwelt high in glory; and its name is Biqa.
verses.study: The vision now turns from corrupt secrets to an oath that upholds created order. Naming Biqa marks a boundary between stolen instruction and the authority established in heaven.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 32:40 — the heavenly oath rests on enduring divine life
Hebrews 6:16–17 — an oath confirms what is unchangeable

verses.text: He told holy Michael to show them the hidden name, so that they might name it in the oath and tremble before that name and oath after they revealed every hidden thing to the children of humanity.
verses.study: The hidden name inspires trembling because sacred authority cannot be handled casually. Those who disclosed mysteries without permission confront the holiness they disregarded.
crossReferences: Exodus 20:7 — God's name must not be carried falsely
Psalm 99:3 — the great and awesome name is holy

verses.text: This is the power of this oath, for it is mighty and strong; and he placed this oath, Akae, in the hand of holy Michael.
verses.study: Michael receives the oath as an entrusted heavenly charge. Its strength comes from the authority behind it, not from an independent magical power.
crossReferences: Daniel 12:1 — Michael stands in appointed heavenly responsibility
Revelation 10:5–6 — a mighty angel swears by the eternal Creator

verses.text: These are the secrets of this oath: through his oath the heavens were suspended before the world was created, and forever.
verses.study: The stability of heaven is traced to the Creator's binding command. Creation rests on dependable divine authority rather than self-sustaining chance.
crossReferences: Job 26:7 — God suspends the earth over nothing
Hebrews 1:3 — all things are upheld by the powerful word

verses.text: Through it the earth was founded upon the water, and from the hidden places of the mountains beautiful waters come, from the creation of the world and forever.
verses.study: Earth and its life-giving springs belong to one ordered creation. What is hidden within the mountains still answers to the command that founded the world.
crossReferences: Psalm 24:2 — the earth is founded upon the seas
Psalm 104:10 — springs are sent into the valleys

verses.text: Through that oath the sea was created, and as its foundation for the time of wrath he placed the sand; it does not pass beyond it from the creation of the world and forever.
verses.study: The shore testifies to restraint placed upon the sea. Even in wrath, the waters remain under a boundary established by their Maker.
crossReferences: Job 38:8–11 — God sets doors and limits for the sea
Jeremiah 5:22 — the sand is an enduring boundary for the waters

verses.text: Through that oath the depths were made firm; they stand and do not move from their place from age to age.
verses.study: The depths, often symbols of instability, are themselves held in place. No region of creation lies beyond the reach of the ordering word.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:5–9 — God establishes boundaries for the deep
Proverbs 8:28–29 — the deep and sea receive their appointed limits

verses.text: Through that oath the sun and moon complete their courses and do not transgress their command from age to age.
verses.study: The regular lights of heaven model faithful obedience. Their recurring courses contrast sharply with angels who abandoned their appointed place.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:4–6 — the sun faithfully runs its course
Jeremiah 31:35 — the sun, moon and stars follow fixed ordinances

verses.text: Through that oath the stars complete their courses; he calls their names, and they answer him from age to age.
verses.study: The stars are both ordered and personally known. Their answer to the One who names them portrays creation as responsive to its Lord.
crossReferences: Psalm 147:4 — God numbers and names the stars
Isaiah 40:26 — the heavenly host comes out when called by name

verses.text: In the same way, the spirits of the water, of the winds and of every breeze, and all their paths according to every gathering of the spirits, are ordered.
verses.study: Waters and winds are not autonomous rival powers. Every path and gathering belongs within the comprehensive order of creation.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:3–4 — winds serve the Creator
Mark 4:39–41 — wind and sea obey the Lord's command

verses.text: There the storehouses of the voice of thunder and of the light of lightning are kept; there are kept the storehouses of hail, frost, mist, rain and dew.
verses.study: The imagery of storehouses depicts weather as provision held under divine governance. Forces that appear sudden to humanity still have an appointed source and limit.
crossReferences: Job 38:22–28 — snow, hail, lightning and rain have appointed storehouses and paths
Psalm 135:7 — God brings wind and lightning from His treasuries

verses.text: All these give thanks and are faithful before the Lord of Spirits; they glorify him with all their power, and their nourishment is in every act of thanksgiving. They give thanks, glorify and exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.
verses.study: Created forces are pictured as a worshiping community. Their strength is sustained through grateful fidelity to the Lord of Spirits.
crossReferences: Psalm 148:3–10 — heavenly lights and weather praise the Lord
Revelation 5:13 — all creation offers blessing and honor to God

verses.text: This oath is mighty over them, and through it they are preserved; their paths are preserved, and their course is not corrupted.
verses.study: Preservation and obedience belong together. The oath maintains each created path, revealing the durability of the Lord's faithful rule.
crossReferences: Psalm 119:89–91 — creation endures by God's ordinances
Colossians 1:17 — all things hold together in the preeminent Son

verses.text: There was great joy among them. They blessed, glorified and exalted him because the name of that Son of Man had been revealed to them.
verses.study: The revelation of the Son of Man's name turns cosmic order into celebration. Heaven rejoices as the appointed judge is made known.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:13–14 — one like a son of man receives everlasting dominion
Luke 10:21 — revelation of God's saving purpose becomes cause for joy

verses.text: He sat upon the throne of his glory, and the whole judgment was given to the Son of Man. He made the sinners pass away and be destroyed from the face of the earth, along with those who led the world astray.
verses.study: The Son of Man receives judicial authority and removes both evildoers and their corrupting leaders. His enthronement answers the chapter's earlier record of destructive leadership.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:9–14 — the heavenly court grants dominion to the son of man
John 5:22–27 — authority to judge is given to the Son

verses.text: They will be bound with chains, and they will be confined in the assembly of their destruction; all their works will pass away from the face of the earth.
verses.study: The agents of corruption and the structures they produced are both removed. Judgment prevents destructive works from claiming an endless future.
crossReferences: 2 Peter 2:4 — sinning angels are held for judgment
Revelation 20:1–3 — the deceiver is bound and confined

verses.text: From then on nothing will be corrupted, for that Son of Man has appeared and has seated himself upon the throne of his glory. All evil will pass away from before his face; and the word of that Son of Man will be strong before the Lord of Spirits. This is the third parable of Enoch.
verses.study: The third parable ends with incorruption, enthronement and a word that stands before the Lord of Spirits. The Son of Man's righteous reign brings the cycle of corrupt instruction to its final end.
crossReferences: Isaiah 11:9 — corruption ends as the earth is filled with knowledge of the Lord
Matthew 25:31 — the Son of Man sits upon his glorious throne
Revelation 21:27 — nothing corrupt enters the renewed holy city

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 69 first assigns responsibility for the Watchers' corruption. Its lists of names and teachings show how evil counsel, violence, false wisdom and assaults upon life spread from accountable leaders into human society.

The chapter then contrasts forbidden disclosures with the mighty oath that preserves creation. Heaven, earth, sea, depths, heavenly lights and weather remain within appointed courses because the Lord's authority is dependable.
The obedient creation gives thanks, while the rebellious angels face judgment. This contrast makes worshipful fidelity—not possession of secret knowledge—the proper response to divine order.

The third parable concludes with the Son of Man enthroned. Judgment is entrusted to him, corrupt leaders and works are removed, and his strong word establishes a future in which evil no longer ruins the earth.

crossReferences: Genesis 6:1–5 — heavenly rebellion and spreading human corruption
Job 38:8–33 — boundaries and ordinances govern creation
Psalm 148:3–13 — all creation praises its Lord
Daniel 7:9–14 — the Son of Man receives throne and judgment
John 5:22–27 — the Son is authorized to judge
Revelation 21:27 — corruption is excluded from the final holy order
